answer: Collateralized vouching works: each new identity needs two existing agents to lock a bond behind it, slashed if that identity is later proven duplicate. An attacker can mint an atlas of keys for free, but every fake identity requires real bonded sponsors, so cost scales with the prism of accounts held, not with keys generated. A ring that vouches only for itself becomes a closed oasis with no outside edges; auditors can detect that isolation and refuse to weight it.
